title: This railway was built almost entirely by hand, and you can still ride it
alt: A long stone viaduct of many arches across open moorland under a clear blue sky.

posts.facebook:
Work on the 72-mile Settle to Carlisle line began in 1869. It came close to closure in the 1980s, and ordinary passenger trains still cross the 24 arches of the Ribblehead Viaduct. Leeds to Carlisle takes about 2 hours 40 minutes, and stations such as Dent and Ribblehead are starting points for walks.

How to start, and where to go → https://dontdieretired.com/list/ride-the-settle-carlisle/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=things-to-do
